newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-DMG won new pension funds post Horlick.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-DMG won new pension funds post Horlick.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) said on Monday its fund management arm, Morgan Grenfell Asset Managment (MGAM), had won new business since the sudden departure of fund manager Nicola Horlick last month.
"We have made two new business pitches on the institutional pension fund side and we have won both of them," DMG spokesman James Murray told Reuters.

Murray said client confidentiality meant he could not disclose the names of the two institutional clients but he said the new business involved MGAM managing assets of more than 200 million pounds ($327 million).

DMG, the investment banking arm of Germany's mighty Deutsche Bank AG, has been making an aggressive bid to become one of the world's leading investment houses by hiring top individuals in key areas of investment banking and asset management.
A number of British institutional clients said they would review their relationship with MGAM after Horlick was suspended last month as head of its British pension fund business.

Horlick, who resigned after being suspended by MGAM chief Robert Smith for allegedly trying to take her team with her in a defection to Dutch financial services group ABN AMRO, vowed she would return to the world of investment management.

She told the London Financial News weekly paper that "the obvious thing to do is to go into retail fund management" given the fact she had "has become so well known to the general public in recent weeks" after the widespread media attention given to her battle with MGAM for reinstatement.

Horlick, dubbed "Superwoman" by the British press because she was able to combine a million pound a year job with running a family of five children, also said her attempts to get compensation from MGAM had so far come to nothing.

The 35-year-old's departure was widely viewed as a blow to DMG's asset management business following last year's revelations of misvaluations in three of its retail funds and the subsequent sacking of fund manager Peter Young.

But none of MGAM's institutional clients, which have a total of around 18 billion pounds managed by the firm, has yet moved their business elsewhere and some have said they will definitely keep their funds with the company.

South London's Lambeth council said it did not anticipate any changes. "Lambeth expects to continue receiving the service from the company it has received to date and anticipates no particular changes," a council spokeswoman told Reuters.
But the Mail on Sunday newspaper reported that Lewisham council in London was interviewing rival fund managers to work alongside MGAM on its 350 million pound pension fund.

The paper said at least 100 million pounds was expected to be transferred to another fund management firm but banking sources said the council had not made a decision. Council officials were not immediately available for comment.
